Protocol cap: because this span coincides with the ch-22 chapter rollup on a marker-rich (q1/q2) chapter, the T423 chapter_only_fallback rule prices the row medium_low and routes it to the low-confidence register and frontier escalation queue for convergence-time review; the cap reflects protocol discipline for chapter-coincident units outside the Psalter, not doubt about the superscription-plus-doxology warrant.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the psalm at its internal stanza seams (e.g. the theophany 22:8-16 or the righteousness recital 22:21-28, where the substrate's blank poetry lines mark strophes) — rejected because every candidate seam lies inside one continuous quoted speech governed by the single superscription frame: strophic articulation is the poem's internal architecture, not a unit boundary, and the campaign keeps superscribed songs whole (1:17-27 precedent; modern strophe divisions are metadata-tier evidence in any case).

boundary_rationale: The testament heading 'Now these are the last words of David' with the fourfold oracle-speaker titulary — son of Jesse, raised on high, anointed of the God of Jacob, sweet psalmist of Israel (web:2Sam.23.1) — opens a self-contained oracle poem: the Spirit-spoke-by-me inspiration claim (web:2Sam.23.2), the quoted divine word on the righteous ruler as morning light (web:2Sam.23.3-4), the everlasting-covenant application 'Isn't my house so with God?' (web:2Sam.23.5), and the antithetic thorns close on the ungodly burned with fire (web:2Sam.23.6-7) — heading, inspiration frame, oracle, application, and antithesis forming one testament unit. An open scribal division after 23:7 (single-witness) stands between testament and roster, where the register heading would divide them anyway.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching the oracle to ch 22 as one poetic diptych — rejected because 23:1 carries its own independent heading formula ('these are the last words') and a different genre (numbered-speaker oracle in Balaam's ne'um-style versus thanksgiving psalm): the two poems are deliberately juxtaposed but formally self-framed, each with its own superscription and closure.

boundary_rationale: The register heading 'These are the names of the mighty men whom David had' (web:2Sam.23.8) opens the roster's first tier -- the Three: Josheb Basshebeth's eight hundred slain 'at one time' (23:8), Eleazar's stand with the frozen sword-hand -- 'when they defied the Philistines who were there gathered together to battle' (web:2Sam.23.9; oshb:2Sam.23.9 בְּחָרְפָם בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּים נֶאֶסְפוּ שָׁם לַמִּלְחָמָה), with no place-name given in either witness -- closing on the refrain 'Yahweh worked a great victory that day' (web:2Sam.23.10), and Shammah's lentil-plot stand closing on the same victory refrain (web:2Sam.23.11-12) -- the doubled refrain (וַיַּעַשׂ יְהוָה תְּשׁוּעָה גְדוֹלָה at 23:10 and again at 23:12) bracketing the tier. The 'After him' chain-formula (וְאַחֲרָיו) opens the second and third entries at 23:9 and 23:11, though not the first, which follows the register heading directly. The tier's entry joints each attract a samekh space in the codex (23:8, 23:10, 23:12, single-witness) — the scribes marking list rhythm the 'After him' formula already beats.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Running the whole roster 23:8-39 as one register -- rejected because the roster's own formula visibly changes register three times: the exploit-prose entries of the Three (8-12), the inset Bethlehem-water narrative (13-17), the second-tier pair with not-attaining-to-the-Three evaluations (18-23), and the bare name-chain of the Thirty (24-39); the campaign splits a list only where the list's own formula changes, and these four formula-blocks are that case.

boundary_rationale: A scene-narrative inset opens with a movement-and-season formula — 'Three of the thirty chief men went down, and came to David in the harvest time to the cave of Adullam' with the Rephaim and Bethlehem garrison staging (web:2Sam.23.13-14) — and runs a complete vignette: David's longing cry for the water of the Bethlehem gate-well (web:2Sam.23.15), the three breaking through the Philistine lines, and the libation refusal 'he would not drink of it, but poured it out to Yahweh' with the blood-of-the-men speech (web:2Sam.23.16-17), closed by the register's colophon 'The three mighty men did these things'. The colophon's close is met by one more closed interval (setumah after 23:17, single-witness).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping the vignette inside the Three's register entry-chain — rejected because 23:13-17 breaks the 'After him' entry-formula entirely: it is anonymous ('three of the thirty'), scene-narrated with dialogue and location staging, and closed by its own colophon; the register's formula change, not the story's content, marks it as a distinct unit between the tiers.

literature_type_guess: heroic_register_with_narrative_insets (Abishai and Benaiah, the second tier)
boundary_rationale: The tier re-opens with a named-chief formula — 'Abishai, the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was chief of the three' with his three-hundred exploit and the rank evaluation 'he wasn't included as one of the three' (web:2Sam.23.18-19) — and pairs him with Benaiah son of Jehoiada: the two-lion-hearted-Moabites, the lion in the pit on the snowy day, and the Egyptian's own-spear kill (web:2Sam.23.20-21), closed by the matching evaluation formula 'he was more honorable than the thirty, but he didn't attain to the three. David set him over his guard' (web:2Sam.23.22-23) — two entries in one evaluative sub-register whose repeated name-among-the-three / not-to-the-three formula binds them. Spacing after 23:19 and 23:23 (samekh, single-witness) shadows the two evaluation formulas that actually articulate this sub-register.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting Abishai and Benaiah into separate decisions — rejected because both entries share one distinctive evaluative formula-pair (had a name among the three; did not attain to the three) that appears nowhere else in the roster: the parallel evaluations are a designed two-panel sub-register, and per the list-register rule entries of one formula stay together.

boundary_rationale: The roster's final formula-block: a bare name-chain opening 'Asahel the brother of Joab was one of the thirty' (web:2Sam.23.24) and running thirty-plus gentilic-tagged names — through Eliam son of Ahithophel (web:2Sam.23.34), Naharai armor-bearer to Joab (23:37) — to the pointed final entry 'and Uriah the Hittite' with the closing count 'thirty-seven in all' (web:2Sam.23.39). The WLC samekh chain marking nearly every name (23:24-39, single-witness) is exactly the case the addendum's weak-corroboration tier plus the list-register rule anticipates: the marks track list-entries, not literary units, and the chain is one cumulative register closed by its own tally formula, its last name (Uriah) a designed echo of the court narrative. WLC petuchah after 23:39 (single-witness, weak corroboration) ends the roster.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the name-chain at the samekh marks or at geographic clusters — rejected as a marker-only claim (insufficient under m8-mesh-r2): no text signal changes anywhere inside the chain (one uniform name-plus-gentilic formula throughout), and the tally 'thirty-seven in all' totals the whole chain as a single register; the only formula change in the roster is at 23:24's entry into bare-list mode, which is this unit's opening edge.

boundary_rationale: The divine-anger formula 'Again Yahweh's anger burned against Israel, and he moved David against them' with the quoted incitement 'Go, count Israel and Judah' (web:2Sam.24.1) opens the command scene: the Dan-to-Beersheba census order to Joab (web:2Sam.24.2), Joab's may-Yahweh-add-a-hundredfold objection 'But why does my lord the king delight in this thing?' (web:2Sam.24.3), and the overruling close 'Notwithstanding, the king's word prevailed against Joab' with the commissioners' exit from the royal presence (web:2Sam.24.4) — command, protest, and prevailing word completing the audience. A samekh interval intrudes after 24:2 (single-witness) while the audience is still in session; the command scene runs through it unbroken.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying the unit into the itinerary 24:5 — rejected because 24:5 opens the field operation with a crossing formula ('They passed over the Jordan and encamped in Aroer') beginning a route register through nine months: court audience and survey itinerary are different registers, seamed at the departure.

boundary_rationale: The crossing formula 'They passed over the Jordan and encamped in Aroer' (web:2Sam.24.5) opens a formal route register — Gilead, Tahtim Hodshi, Dan Jaan, around to Sidon, the stronghold of Tyre, out to Beersheba (web:2Sam.24.6-7) — closed by the duration notice 'nine months and twenty days' (web:2Sam.24.8) and the tally report formula 'Joab gave up the sum of the counting of the people to the king… eight hundred thousand… and five hundred thousand' (web:2Sam.24.9) — circuit and census-total forming one register unit whose numbers trigger the crisis.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching the tally 24:9 to the remorse scene it provokes — rejected because 24:9 is the register's own closing formula (the sum delivered is the census's completion, in report register), while 24:10 opens with an interior-state formula ('David's heart struck him after he had counted') beginning the penitence dialogue: the register closes with its total, per the tally-close precedent of 23:39.

boundary_rationale: The interior-state formula 'David's heart struck him after he had counted the people' with the I-have-sinned-greatly confession (web:2Sam.24.10) opens the judgment dialogue: the morning word-event to Gad the seer (web:2Sam.24.11-12, prophetic word formula 'Yahweh's word came to the prophet Gad'), the three-options oracle — famine, flight, or pestilence — with Gad's answer-demand (web:2Sam.24.13), and David's choice 'Let us fall now into Yahweh's hand, for his mercies are great. Let me not fall into man's hand' (web:2Sam.24.14) — confession, offer, and election completing the exchange. This dialogue's turns are each spaced in the codex — closed after 24:10, open after 24:11, closed again after 24:13 (single-witness) — one more case of layout keeping time with speech rather than marking units.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the Gad word-event 24:11-13 from the confession 24:10 — rejected because the confession's put-away-iniquity petition is answered directly by the morning oracle (petition and response form one judicial exchange, as at 12:13-14), and the choice at 24:14 answers the question posed at 24:13; the unit's arc runs sin-confessed to sentence-chosen without a scene change.

literature_type_guess: narrative_prose (pestilence, relenting, and the shepherd's intercession)
boundary_rationale: The execution formula 'So Yahweh sent a pestilence on Israel from the morning even to the appointed time' with the seventy-thousand toll (web:2Sam.24.15) opens the plague panel: the angel's outstretched hand over Jerusalem, the relenting 'It is enough. Now withdraw your hand', and the location fix 'by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite' (web:2Sam.24.16), closed by David's intercession at the sight of the angel — 'I have sinned… but these sheep, what have they done? Please let your hand be against me' (web:2Sam.24.17) — the shepherd-king offering himself, which the altar command answers. The panel's joints are traced by a samekh after 24:16 and an open break after 24:17 (single-witness), scribal punctuation under the theophany's own hinges.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching the intercession 24:17 to the altar-command unit 24:18-25 — rejected because 24:17 is spoken at the plague's climax 'when he saw the angel who struck the people' (the same visionary moment as 24:16's threshing-floor scene), while 24:18 opens a new day and a new speech-event ('Gad came that day to David and said'): the intercession belongs to the crisis it answers, the altar to its resolution.

literature_type_guess: narrative_dialogue (the threshing-floor purchase and the altar)
boundary_rationale: The prophetic command formula 'Gad came that day to David and said to him, Go up, build an altar to Yahweh on the threshing floor of Araunah' (web:2Sam.24.18) opens the resolution scene: the obedient ascent (24:19), Araunah's obeisance and why-has-my-lord-come question (web:2Sam.24.20-21), the offered oxen and sledges with the give-it-all speech (web:2Sam.24.22-23), David's refusal 'I will not offer burnt offerings to Yahweh my God which cost me nothing' with the fifty-shekel purchase (web:2Sam.24.24), and the altar's burnt and peace offerings closing on 'So Yahweh was entreated for the land, and the plague was removed from Israel' (web:2Sam.24.25) — a final entreated-for-the-land formula that both ends the census arc and, echoing 21:14 verbatim in structure, closes the appendix's framing pair and the book. One last closed interval falls inside the purchase negotiation (after 24:23, single-witness); the entreated-for-the-land formula, not the spacing, ends the book.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the purchase negotiation 24:20-24 from the altar notice 24:25 — rejected because the negotiation's entire purpose clause ('to buy your threshing floor, to build an altar to Yahweh, that the plague may be stopped', 24:21) is discharged only by 24:25's built altar and stayed plague: command, purchase, and offering form one obedience arc at one location, and the entreated-formula is its designed close.
